title: Minimax Detection Radius for Arbitrary Treatment Effects in Low-Rank Staggered Gaussian Panels
banked_reason: D0.5 score gate capped the balanced rank-one one-quadrant result at incremental (paper-score ceiling 5.6), below the field floor; a genuine multi-chart matched frontier is an unbounded new program, and the WSVD Taylor-curvature proof remains unestablished.
gap_reasons: The matched result is confined to a balanced square panel, rank one, one missing quadrant, and fixed interior incoherence; the general staggered multi-chart frontier and shrinking-incoherence regime remain open, so the note does not deliver a frontier for staggered low-rank panels broadly.

The displayed Taylor audit treats the core pseudoinverse as an ordinary inverse on fixed rank-one spaces; for Π_1(B)^† it omits the subspace/projection-curvature remainder from DΠ_1 and the corresponding Moore--Penrose projector terms, so the asserted C_0τ_n^2(δ̂_n^{-1}+M̂_nδ̂_n^{-2}+M̂_n^2δ̂_n^{-3}) bound is not reproduced.
The ATT proposition transfers coverage by norm duality but supplies neither an optimal-length result nor evidence that the resulting interval is practically competitive.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a balanced rank-one, one-missing-quadrant interior frontier of order σ√n and a sharp μ=1 boundary phase, then attempted to lift the construction to an observable wedge-aware certificate. The field-level program collapsed because the genuine multi-chart synchronization and matching packing remained open, while the balanced WSVD upper proof still omitted singular-subspace and Moore--Penrose curvature terms. A future run should reuse the endpoint packings and boundary geometry but independently rebuild the transport perturbation argument before claiming honesty.
tldr: The paper indexes the Gaussian panel experiment by admissible tuples \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\), so the latent counterfactual matrix remains part of the experiment index even when tuples induce the same observed law. Its principal proved benchmark is the balanced rank-one L-mask rate \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\sqrt n\) at each fixed \(\mu>1\), established by an all-procedure lower bound and a total polynomial-time one-block certificate whose conditional Gaussian, finite-simulation, homogeneous Taylor, and fallback contributions are controlled separately. Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} is the boundary companion for every \(0<\kappa\le1\): at \(\mu=1\), both normalized balanced overlap Grams equal one, the matching rate is \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\) when \(s_-<s_+\), and the radius is exactly zero when \(s_-=s_+\), even though \(\mathfrak R_n\ge\sigma\sqrt{2n}\). Thus neither the fixed-\mu>1 rate nor a tangent-modulus lower comparison extends to the saturated boundary. The shrinking-incoherence layer and multi-chart patterns beyond the proved one-block case remain open in Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge}. The diffuse-weight ATT interval is only a coverage-valid duality corollary.
gap: Sharp staggered-panel inference is coordinatewise or functional-specific, while global matrix confidence theory uses random or isotropic measurements. No located result gives a tuple-indexed honest nuclear ball under a deterministic adoption wedge with a computable spectral radius and an all-procedure benchmark.
fill: The principal theorem proves the \(\sigma\sqrt n\) two-sided frontier. Its total spectral certificate is audited term by term, including a squared synchronization amplification in the homogeneous Taylor remainder and a genuine large-gap fallback tail. The overlap-aligned tangent-packing question isolates the unmatched arbitrary-wedge extension.
